9: # How a run works
10: 
11: > In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
12: 
13: A run is one attempt at one scenario of one challenge. It starts with a run token, gives your agent a task and
14: logins for the challenge's websites, and ends when your agent submits its answer or time runs out. Test runs and
15: scored runs both run your package in the [sandbox](#scored-run); you develop on your own machine with the scouting
16: logins.
17: 
18: ## Develop locally, then test in the sandbox
19: 
20: RFQ has one public scenario, `public-1`: the websites as you see them.
21: 
22: 1. **Develop locally** against the public websites with the scouting logins the organizers publish:
23:    `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` (in PowerShell: `atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`) sets
24:    `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the websites and their logins, the JSON a run gets), each website's URL as
25:    `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL`, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the `brief`, `access`, `submission` and `answer_schema` of
26:    `GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` as JSON (`CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` is that address). There is no run token.
27:    Where the platform hosts models, they need no key: `--env` also exports each one's base URL and key, pointed at
28:    `atira models proxy` on your computer with `local` as the key, so run `atira login` once, then keep
29:    `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. Those calls are free, recorded and never ranked. Any other
30:    provider takes your own key.
31:    Nothing done with these logins counts.
32:    A bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.
33: 2. **Test in the sandbox:** `atira test-run ./my-agent` uploads your package, starts a test run on `public-1` and
34:    opens its run page live. It runs in the same sandbox as a scored run, but for up to 2 hours instead of 20 minutes (keep it under
35:    20 to be safe), and the run page shows its
36:    score with the full breakdown. `atira cancel` stops it early.
37: 
38: ## Inside a run
39: 
40: 1. **Read the task:** `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with the header `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`
41:    returns:
42:    - `brief`: the task statement in markdown, with the rules;
43:    - `access`: one entry per website: `siteId`, `url`, and `credentials` (`username`, `password`);
44:    - `submission`: where the answer goes: `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` (POST it to that URL) or
45:      `{"kind": "site", "siteId": ..., "url": ...}` (submit it on that website, e.g. RFQ's configurator);
46:    - `answer_url` (API submissions only) and `answer_schema` (JSON Schema of the answer);
47:    - `started_at`, `expires_at`, and what the run has spent on LLM calls so far.
48:    - `llm_proxy_url`: the model proxy base with this run's token, `llm_providers` and `llm_base_urls` (each
49:      provider's proxy base), and `llm_env` (the SDK base-URL variables the run step gets).
50:    Keep the token secret: it is your agent's identity for this run.
51: 2. **Work:** your agent logs into the websites with those credentials and collects what it needs. Its LLM calls
52:    go through our metering proxy: a hosted model's with the run token its key variable already holds, any other
53:    provider's with your own key (below).
54: 3. **Answer** through the run's `submission` target. For an `api` target, `POST` the answer as JSON to
55:    `answer_url` with the same `x-api-key` header. For a `site` target, submit it on that website: the site
56:    forwards it to the platform, shows the same validation issues in German, and confirms with a receipt.
57:    - `400` with `issues`: the answer is malformed. Nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running, fix it and send
58:      it again.
59:    - `202`: accepted and final. The run ends, the token and the website logins stop working, and a test run
60:      returns its score and breakdown. Your agent then has 10 seconds to exit before the platform stops it.
61: 
62: Site logins are issued per run and only work while that run is live. Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header
63: (`Authorization: Bearer` works too). Send a User-Agent of your own: the edge in
64: front of the API currently refuses Python's default `Python-urllib/…` agent with 403. Test runs last up to 2 hours.
65: 
66: ## LLM calls
67: 
68: Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
69: Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
70: own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
71: API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.
72: 
73: The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:
74: 
75: ```
76: $API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
77: ```
78: 
79: `llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:
80: 
81: | Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
82: | --- | --- | --- |
83: | `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
84: | `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
85: | `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
86: | `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
87: | `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
88: | `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
89: | `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
90: | `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
91: | `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
92: | `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |
93: 
94: The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
95: each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
96: (messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.
97: 
98: ### Your key
99: 
100: Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
101: (OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
102: unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
103: not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.
104: 
105: With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
106: `OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
107: as `x-api-key`:
108: 
109: ```python
110: from openai import OpenAI
111: 
112: client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
113: ```
114: 
115: A client that cannot set the provider's own header may send the key as `x-provider-key`; the proxy forwards it in
116: the provider's header. For Google's Gemini SDK, set the HTTP base URL explicitly:
117: 
118: ```python
119: import os
120: from google import genai
121: 
122: client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
123:     http_options={"base_url": os.environ["LLM_PROXY_URL"] + "/google"})
124: ```
125: 
126: ```javascript
127: import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"
128: 
129: const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
130:   httpOptions: { baseUrl: process.env.LLM_PROXY_URL + "/google" } })
131: ```
132: 
133: A request without a key of its own gets `401` "Add your <provider> API key to the request.", unless the
134: organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
135: key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
136: start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.
137: 
138: **Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
139: `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
140: (prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
141: for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
142: `x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
143: `401`.
144: 
145: A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
146: context.
147: 
148: ### How cost is measured
149: 
150: Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
151: provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
152: An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
153: `"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
154: that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
155: a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
156: providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
157: chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
158: an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up
159: early is still billed for everything the provider sends. There is no spending limit. Model listings and other
160: endpoints without inference usage cost nothing; Anthropic `count_tokens` also costs nothing. All network and
161: fair-play rules still apply, including when using provider-side tools.
162: 
163: The models the platform hosts itself (`GET /v1/models/status` lists them with their prices) are free to use, never
164: charged; each call counts toward your run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest.
165: 
166: ### Team secrets
167: 
168: Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test runs and scored runs, such as
169: `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token:
170: 
171: ```sh
172: curl -X PUT -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
173:   --data '{"value": "sk-…"}' "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
174: curl -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets"   # names and dates only
175: curl -X DELETE -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
176: ```
177: 
178: Values are encrypted, never shown again and redacted from run logs; saving a name again replaces its value.
179: Setup never receives them. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and
180: cannot be platform variables (`CHALLENGE_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `*_SERVER_URL`, `*_PROXY`, `LLM_PROXY_URL`,
181: `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `PATH`, `HOME`, `DISPLAY`, …). A team keeps at most 20; each value is 16 characters to 4 KB long.
182: 
183: ## Scored run
184: 
185: Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run
186: ranks on the leaderboard. The final run at the end of the hackathon uses the same sandbox on a private dataset (see
187: [Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md#what-happens-next)). Runs are created from your uploaded package. The sandbox is
188: a Linux VM with a desktop at 1280×800, a **headful Chromium** already open with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on
189: `127.0.0.1:9222` (or up to four, see [Browsers](#browsers)) and these toolchains, ready for your user:
190: 
191: - **TypeScript and JavaScript:** Node 24 (runs `.ts` files directly), npm, pnpm and bun.
192: - **Python:** Python 3.12 and uv (`uv venv`, `uv pip install`, `uv run`); there is no system pip.
193: - **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
194:   and the websites.
195: - gcc, make, git, curl and jq.
196: 
197: 1. **Setup (not counted toward your time, up to 5 minutes):** your `setup` command runs with network access but without any credentials, e.g. to install dependencies.
198: 2. **Model warm-up (not counted toward your time):** the models the platform hosts itself, when it offers any, scale
199:    to zero when nobody uses them, and waking one takes one to eight minutes. The platform wakes them as soon as your
200:    run leaves the queue and starts your run only once they're warm (at most 10 minutes after setup), so a cold start
201:    never counts toward your time. The run's log says when they're warm. While runs are active, the platform keeps
202:    them warm. `"models"` in `agent.json` lists the ones your agent system calls, by their `provider` id from
203:    `GET /v1/models/status` (the start page shows it too); the run waits for those alone, and `"models": []` starts it
204:    right after setup:
205: 
206:    ```json
207:    {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": []}
208:    ```
209: 
210:    Without it the run waits for every hosted model. Anything else, such as an unknown id, rejects the package with
211:    `Invalid agent.json: models: …` and the ids it takes. It decides only the wait: your run may call any hosted model
212:    whatever it lists, but one it didn't list may still be waking.
213: 
214:    **If a hosted model fails mid-run:** retry failed calls, as with any provider; a short outage is yours to ride out.
215:    If our models were down for most of the run (from the first failed call on, a 5xx from our model or a lost
216:    connection to it, at least 8 in 10 of the run's hosted-model calls failed, over at least half its time) and the run
217:    then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count toward ranking or
218:    any limit, and a scored run starts again once by itself. A
219:    run that answered keeps its result.
220: 3. **Run (timed):** your `run` command starts with this environment. The clock starts here.
221: 
222: | Variable | Value |
223: | --- | --- |
224: | `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the API; read your task at `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` |
225: | `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | the run token |
226: | `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON: the same as `access` |
227: | `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
228: | `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`, `<MODEL>_API_KEY` | for each model the platform hosts (`GET /v1/models/status`; the start page names them): its base URL through the proxy, under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>`, and the run token as its key |
229: | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
230: | `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
231: | `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google`; set the Gemini SDK's HTTP base URL explicitly as above |
232: | `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral`, `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
233: | your [team secrets](#team-secrets) | for example `OPENAI_API_KEY` with your own key |
234: | `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222`, browser 1 |
235: | `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: `["http://127.0.0.1:9222"]` for one browser |
236: | `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started: `1` unless `agent.json` asks for more |
237: | `DISPLAY` | `:1`, browser 1's screen; browser n is on `:n` |
238: | `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase) | `http://127.0.0.1:3128`, the only way out of the sandbox |
239: | `NO_PROXY` | `localhost,127.0.0.1` (CDP stays local) |
240: 
241: The platform sets no API key variables of its own, except the run-token placeholder for a provider the
242: organizers pay for (above). `setup` runs first, with network (install your dependencies there) but without the
243: run's variables or your team secrets, and nothing it starts survives into the run. The run itself reaches only our API and the challenge's websites,
244: through that proxy; Chromium is already configured to use it. A scored run of RFQ has 20 minutes; a run that
245: ends without an answer scores 0.
246: 
247: ## Browsers
248: 
249: The sandbox starts one browser unless `agent.json` asks for more, up to four:
250: 
251: ```json
252: {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "browsers": 3}
253: ```
254: 
255: `browsers` is a whole number from 1 to 4; anything else rejects the package with
256: `Invalid agent.json: browsers: must be a whole number from 1 to 4`. Browser n is its own headful Chromium with its
257: own profile, on display `:n` (1280×800) with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on port 9221 + n (9222 to 9225), behind
258: the same proxy as browser 1. All of them are ready before the clock starts. `CDP_URL` stays browser 1, `CDP_URLS` lists all of
259: them in order, and `BROWSER_COUNT` says how many there are. With three:
260: 
261: | Variable | Value |
262: | --- | --- |
263: | `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222` |
264: | `CDP_URLS` | `["http://127.0.0.1:9222","http://127.0.0.1:9223","http://127.0.0.1:9224"]` |
265: | `BROWSER_COUNT` | `3` |
266: 
267: **At most 4 browsers run at a time:** ask for up to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts
268: inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The scored sandbox enforces it:
269: any other browser the agent starts is stopped within seconds, and the run's logs say so with
270: `[platform] stopped a browser the agent started: at most 4 run at a time; use the browsers from CDP_URLS`. Every
271: browser then is one the platform can show and record: test runs show them side by side while they run, with a
272: recording of each afterwards.
273: 
274: On your own machine, developing with the scouting logins, `CDP_URLS` is not set and your agent starts its own
275: browsers.

9: # Debug runs from your coding agent
10: 
11: > In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
12: 
13: `atira mcp` makes the CLI an MCP server, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other coding agents can read your runs
14: and debug them with you: find the failing step in the logs, see the browser's screen at that moment, check what the
15: agent clicked and typed, then start the next test run. It uses the CLI's sign-in, so there is nothing new to set up.
16: 
17: ## Set it up
18: 
19: Install the CLI and sign in once ([CLI guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)):
20: 
21: ```sh
22: curl -fsSL $API/install.sh | sh
23: atira login
24: ```
25: 
26: Then add the server to your coding agent:
27: 
28: ```sh
29: claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp     # Claude Code
30: codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp      # Codex
31: ```
32: 
33: Other clients (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, ...) take the usual `mcpServers` entry:
34: 
35: ```json
36: { "mcpServers": { "atira": { "command": "atira", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
37: ```
38: 
39: For Codex you can also write it in `~/.codex/config.toml`:
40: 
41: ```toml
42: [mcp_servers.atira]
43: command = "atira"
44: args = ["mcp"]
45: ```
46: 
47: If your editor can't find `atira`, give its full path: `command -v atira` prints it. `ATIRA_TOKEN` works instead of
48: the stored sign-in, and `atira mcp --help` prints these lines.
49: 
50: ## Tools
51: 
52: | Tool | What it does | About |
53: | --- | --- | --- |
54: | `challenge_brief` | The challenge: task, websites, rules and limits, run contract, scoring and answer schema | 6k tokens |
55: | `list_runs` | Your team's recent test and scored runs: status, quality, cost, time and package | 50 tokens a run |
56: | `get_run` | One run: status and failure, queue place or warm-up while it waits, phases, package, model calls by model with failures and queue waits, points per field, recordings, answer, run page | 1–2k |
57: | `diagnose_run` | Why a run failed and whether to rerun it as it is: the failure class, the last 20 stdout and stderr lines, model errors, idle stretches over 60 s, browsers whose screen froze | 2–3k |
58: | `run_logs` | Log lines in time order, by time (`from`, `to`), stream, text (`grep`) and `browser`; `tail` for the last lines; page by page | 30 a line |
59: | `run_llm_calls` | Every model call, one line each, under a header with time in calls, p50/p95 latency, the most calls at once, failures by status and, for models the organizers host, the queue wait | 35 a call |
60: | `run_profile` | Where the time went, per 30 s, 1 min or 5 min: inputs and screen activity per browser, model calls, seconds and cost; then the critical path | 1.5–3k |
61: | `run_screenshot` | A browser's screen at a time with the clicks just before it marked, every browser at once (`browser: "all"`), or a filmstrip (`frames`) | 1.5k an image |
62: | `run_inputs` | The clicks, scrolls and typing the platform recorded in each browser, with their times | 25 an input |
63: | `compare_runs` | Two runs side by side: package, quality, time, cost, cost × time, calls and failures per model, phases, points per field and answer fields that changed | 1–2k |
64: | `wait_for_run` | Wait until a run is running or done, including recording collection and scoring (at most `timeout_s`, default 50 s), then say how it stands | 300 |
65: | `list_submissions` | Your scored submissions: review status, any organizer note, result and package | 60 a submission |
66: | `get_submission` | One submission (`sub_...`): review status, any organizer note, its runs | 300–800 |
67: | `run_package` | The package a run or submission used, as uploaded: SHA-256, label, agent.json and each file's size, never the contents; `out` saves the `.tar.gz` in a folder | 15 a file |
68: | `leaderboard` | The board with each entry's cost × time and the Pareto front, your rank and the gap to the next; `compare_run` places one of your runs on it | 500 |
69: | `models` | The models the organizers host, if any, and how to call them from your computer through `atira models proxy` | 300 |
70: | `test_run` | Pack a folder and start a test run; returns its id, queue place, package SHA-256 and label (the git commit by default) | 150 |
71: | `cancel_run` | Cancel one of your runs that hasn't finished; only with `confirm: true` | 60 |
72: | `submit` | Pack a folder and submit it for a scored run, public and final; only with `confirm: true` after the person said yes | 100 |
73: 
74: Everything only reads, except `test_run`, `cancel_run` and `submit`, and `run_package` with `out`, which saves a file on your computer. A scored submission is public and can't be undone, and a cancelled run
75: doesn't come back, so `submit` and `cancel_run` refuse unless the call says `confirm: true`: tell your agent to ask
76: you first. Your agent sees only what your team sees on the run page; another team's run is "404: run not found".
77: 
78: Run tools take a run id (`run_...`), a test run id (`reh_...`) or a submission id (`sub_...`, meaning its latest run).
79: `run_package` takes the same ids; a submission id there means the package it submitted, which its runs ran.
80: 
81: ## What it shows
82: 
83: `get_run` while a run waits, then once it failed:
84: 
85: ```
86: run_8af0981b3710558a · test run on the public dataset · package 3f2a1c9e0b12 (2 files) "a41c2d9-dirty"
87: Status queued, phase queued
88: Queued: 2 runs ahead of yours, starts in about 3 min
89: ...
90: Status failed, phase done · Failure: Run exited with code 0 without submitting an answer (no answer)
91: ```
92: 
93: `run_llm_calls`:
94: 
95: ```
96: run_0d7f1203b576189a · 86 model calls in a run of 16:22 · $0.4130
97: Time in calls 6:41 · latency p50 2.1s, p95 31s · at most 4 at once (at 02:13)
98:   anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5: 33 calls, $0.4126, 57,619 in (72,128 cached) / 5,867 out, 2:05 in calls
99:   openai/gpt-5-mini: 1 call, $0.0004, 1,845 in / 12 out, 1.2s in calls
100: Failures: openai: 52 failed (429 rate limited)
101: 
102: [02:10.4 +3.2s] anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 200 in 4,210 (cached 3,900) out 312 $0.00471 id=c_812
103: [02:13.9 +0.4s] openai 429 rate limited $0.00 id=c_815
104: ```
105: 
106: `run_profile` (the screen columns are seconds the browser's screen was changing; `–` is still):
107: 
108: ```
109: time   b1 in · screen  b2 in · screen  b3 in · screen  b4 in · screen  calls  in calls  busy  cost
110: 02:00  6 · 21s         3 · 8.0s        10 · 44s        0 · –           14     1:02      48s   $0.0612
111: 03:00  4 · 12s         0 · –           0 · –           2 · 3.5s        3      41s       38s   $0.0140
112: Critical path:
113: Longest stretches over 10 s with no input, no screen change and no model call in flight:
114:   03:12.4–04:40.1 (01:27)
115:     last line before: [03:11.9] stdout: mail TAN: waiting for the TAN message
116: Browsers that went quiet:
117:   browser 3: last screen change at 02:45.4, then nothing for 04:53 until the end
118: ```
119: 
120: `diagnose_run` names the failure's class and the next step: `cancelled`, `no answer` (your agent system ended
121: without entering one: fix it, a rerun alone won't help), `agent exit` (see stderr), `timeout` (make it faster),
122: `answer rejected` (fix the answer's shape) or `platform` (not your agent system: rerun it as it is). A reason that
123: starts with "Setup" is agent.json's setup: `run_logs` with stream `setup` shows why. Where the platform records a
124: run's failure class, that one is used.
125: 
126: ## Times
127: 
128: Times are on the run's clock, as the run page shows them: `02:13`, `1:02:13`, `3m20s` or `133` seconds from the
129: run's start, or an ISO 8601 time; durations are written the same way. The same time in the run page's address,
130: `?t=02:13`, opens the replay there. Links point at the platform's own address, whichever name the CLI talks to.
131: 
132: A screenshot is cut from the recording with ffmpeg on the platform. If the platform can't do that right now, the
133: CLI cuts it with your own ffmpeg (`brew install ffmpeg`, or `sudo apt install ffmpeg`); without one it says so and
134: links the replay. A time outside a recording gets its nearest frame and says so ("browser 1's recording covers
135: -00:03.7–07:48.9").
136: 
137: ## What it can't do
138: 
139: - **Past frames of a live run.** The recording is stored after the run ends and collection finishes; until then `run_screenshot` shows each
140:   browser's latest live frame, about a second behind the screen (its time says when), and
141:   filmstrips and screen activity wait for the end. The run page's live view shows it moving.
142: - **Logs as they arrive.** Tools answer once; `wait_for_run` waits up to 600 s if your client allows long tool calls
143:   (Codex stops a tool after 60 s unless you raise `tool_timeout_sec`). In a terminal, `atira logs <run> --follow`
144:   streams a run's logs until it ends.
145: - **Log streams** are `setup`, `stdout`, `stderr` and `input`: errors are in `stderr` and in `get_run`/`diagnose_run`,
146:   screen activity is in `run_profile`.
147: - **Typed secrets.** Inputs show typed text with keys, tokens and your run's secrets masked.
148: 
149: From a terminal, `atira cancel <run>` cancels a run and `atira status` lists your submissions and test runs.
150: 
151: ## Try it
152: 
153: Ask your agent things like:
154: 
155: - "Why did my last test run fail? Diagnose it, then show me the screen at the moment it went idle."
156: - "Where did the time go in run_19932ad4ade523e4? Which model calls were slowest?"
157: - "Compare my last two test runs: what changed in the score and the cost?"
158: - "Start a test run of ./my-agent, wait until it's running, and show me every browser's screen at 01:00."
159: - "Which files did my latest submission's package have? Save it to ./downloaded and diff it against ./my-agent."
160: 
161: This guide is at `$API/docs/mcp.md`.
162:

1: # MCP Servers (`mcp_config.json`)
2: 
3: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables developers to
4: build secure, two-way integrations between AI models and their data/tools. In
5: Antigravity, configuring MCP servers allows you to expose custom tools,
6: resources, and prompts to the agent.
7: 
8: MCP servers can be configured globally or packaged within plugins.
9: 
10: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
11: 
12: ## Configuration File (`mcp_config.json`)
13: 
14: MCP servers are defined in a `mcp_config.json` file. The file contains a map of
15: server identifiers to their respective configurations.
16: 
17: ### Location
18: 
19: *   **Global Configuration**: `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` (applies to all
20:     sessions).
21: *   **Plugin Configuration**: `plugins/<plugin_name>/mcp_config.json` (active
22:     when the plugin is enabled).
23: 
24: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
25: 
26: ## Configuration Schema
27: 
28: Antigravity supports two transport mechanisms for MCP: **Stdio** (for local
29: command-line tools) and **SSE** (for remote services).
30: 
31: ```json
32: {
33:   "mcpServers": {
34:     "sqlite-helper": {
35:       "command": "sqlite-mcp-server",
36:       "args": ["/path/to/database.db"],
37:       "env": {
38:         "DB_READONLY": "true"
39:       }
40:     },
41:     "remote-service": {
42:       "serverUrl": "https://mcp.mycompany.com/sse"
43:     }
44:   }
45: }
46: ```
47: 
48: ### 1. Stdio Transport (Local)
49: 
50: Used to run a local executable or script as an MCP server. The Language Server
51: spawns the process and communicates with it over standard input/output.
52: 
53: *   **`command`** (string, required): The executable to run (e.g., `node`,
54:     `python3`, or a binary name).
55: *   **`args`** (array of strings, optional): Arguments to pass to the command.
56: *   **`env`** (object, optional): Environment variables to inject into the
57:     server process.
58: 
59: ### 2. SSE Transport (Remote)
60: 
61: Used to connect to a remote MCP server over HTTP using Server-Sent Events (SSE).
62: 
63: *   **`serverUrl`** (string, required): The HTTP(S) URL of the remote MCP
64:     endpoint.
65: 
66: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
67: 
68: ## How the Agent Uses MCP
69: 
70: Once an MCP server is configured and successfully connected:
71: 
72: 1.  **Tool Discovery**: The system queries the server for its available tools.
73: 2.  **Tool Injection**: Discovered tools are automatically added to the agent's
74:     toolset and listed in the system prompt.
75: 3.  **Execution**: When the agent calls an MCP tool, the Language Server routes
76:     the request to the MCP server, executes it, and returns the result to the
77:     agent.
78: 
79: ## Scoping and Scannability
80: 
81: *   **Global Servers**: Active for all conversations.
82: *   **Plugin Servers**: Only active when the parent plugin is loaded. Their
83:     tools are automatically prefixed or namespaced if necessary to avoid
84:     conflicts.
85: *   You can inspect active MCP servers and their tools in the UI by navigating
86:     to **Additional Options (...) > MCP Servers**.
87:

import asyncio
import json
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

SCOUTING_FILE = Path(__file__).parent / "scouting.json"

async def scout_site(playwright, site_info: dict):
    site_id = site_info["siteId"]
    url = site_info["url"]
    creds = site_info["credentials"]
    browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    context = await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 800})
    page = await context.new_page()
    out = {"siteId": site_id, "url": url, "steps": []}
    try:
        resp = await page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=30000)
        await page.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        title = await page.title()
        html_text = await page.evaluate("""() => {
            const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a, button, input, select, textarea, h1, h2, h3, label, th, td, [role="button"]'));
            return els.slice(0, 150).map(e => ({
                tag: e.tagName.toLowerCase(),
                type: e.getAttribute('type') || '',
                name: e.getAttribute('name') || '',
                id: e.id || '',
                placeholder: e.getAttribute('placeholder') || '',
                href: e.getAttribute('href') || '',
                text: (e.innerText || e.value || '').trim().slice(0, 120)
            }));
        }""")
        body_text = await page.evaluate("() => document.body.innerText.slice(0, 4000)")
        out["steps"].append({
            "phase": "landing",
            "status": resp.status if resp else None,
            "current_url": page.url,
            "title": title,
            "body_text": body_text,
            "elements": html_text
        })
    except Exception as e:
        out["error"] = str(e)
    finally:
        await browser.close()
    return out

async def main():
    data = json.loads(SCOUTING_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    async with async_playwright() as pw:
        results = await asyncio.gather(*(scout_site(pw, s) for s in data["access"]))
    out_path = Path(__file__).parent / "scout_landing.json"
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print("Saved scout_landing.json for", [r["siteId"] for r in results])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

import asyncio
import json
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

SCOUTING_FILE = Path(__file__).parent / "scouting.json"

async def extract_page(page, phase: str):
    await page.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    title = await page.title()
    elements = await page.evaluate("""() => {
        const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a, button, input, select, textarea, h1, h2, h3, h4, iframe, [role="button"], [role="tab"]'));
        return els.slice(0, 200).map(e => ({
            tag: e.tagName.toLowerCase(),
            type: e.getAttribute('type') || '',
            name: e.getAttribute('name') || '',
            id: e.id || '',
            placeholder: e.getAttribute('placeholder') || '',
            href: e.getAttribute('href') || '',
            src: e.getAttribute('src') || '',
            text: (e.innerText || e.value || '').trim().replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, 140)
        }));
    }""")
    body_text = await page.evaluate("() => document.body.innerText.slice(0, 6000)")
    return {
        "phase": phase,
        "current_url": page.url,
        "title": title,
        "body_text": body_text,
        "elements": elements
    }

async def scout_site(playwright, site_info: dict):
    site_id = site_info["siteId"]
    url = site_info["url"]
    creds = site_info["credentials"]
    browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    context = await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 800})
    page = await context.new_page()
    out = {"siteId": site_id, "url": url, "steps": []}
    try:
        await page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=30000)
        await page.fill('input[name="username"]', creds["username"])
        await page.fill('input[name="password"]', creds["password"])
        await page.click('button[type="submit"]')
        await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=30000)
        out["steps"].append(await extract_page(page, "post_login"))
    except Exception as e:
        out["error"] = str(e)
    finally:
        await browser.close()
    return out

async def main():
    data = json.loads(SCOUTING_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    async with async_playwright() as pw:
        results = await asyncio.gather(*(scout_site(pw, s) for s in data["access"]))
    out_path = Path(__file__).parent / "scout_post_login.json"
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print("Saved scout_post_login.json for", [r["siteId"] for r in results])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

import asyncio
import json
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

SCOUTING_FILE = Path(__file__).parent / "scouting.json"

async def extract_page(page, phase: str):
    await page.wait_for_timeout(1200)
    title = await page.title()
    elements = await page.evaluate("""() => {
        const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a, button, input, select, textarea, h1, h2, h3, h4, iframe, [role="button"], [role="tab"]'));
        return els.slice(0, 250).map(e => ({
            tag: e.tagName.toLowerCase(),
            type: e.getAttribute('type') || '',
            name: e.getAttribute('name') || '',
            id: e.id || '',
            placeholder: e.getAttribute('placeholder') || '',
            href: e.getAttribute('href') || '',
            src: e.getAttribute('src') || '',
            text: (e.innerText || e.value || '').trim().replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, 160)
        }));
    }""")
    body_text = await page.evaluate("() => document.body.innerText.slice(0, 8000)")
    return {
        "phase": phase,
        "current_url": page.url,
        "title": title,
        "body_text": body_text,
        "elements": elements
    }

async def scout_site(playwright, site_info: dict):
    site_id = site_info["siteId"]
    url = site_info["url"]
    creds = site_info["credentials"]
    browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    context = await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 800})
    page = await context.new_page()
    out = {"siteId": site_id, "url": url, "steps": []}
    try:
        await page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=30000)
        await page.fill('input[name="username"]', creds["username"])
        await page.fill('input[name="password"]', creds["password"])
        await page.locator('button[type="submit"]', has_text="Anmelden").click()
        await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=30000)
        
        # Pass cookie consent wall if present
        cookie_btn = page.locator('button[type="submit"]', has_text="Cookies akzeptieren")
        if await cookie_btn.count() > 0:
            await cookie_btn.first.click()
            await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=30000)

        out["steps"].append(await extract_page(page, "dashboard"))
    except Exception as e:
        out["error"] = str(e)
    finally:
        await browser.close()
    return out

async def main():
    data = json.loads(SCOUTING_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    async with async_playwright() as pw:
        results = await asyncio.gather(*(scout_site(pw, s) for s in data["access"]))
    out_path = Path(__file__).parent / "scout_dashboard.json"
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print("Saved scout_dashboard.json for", [r["siteId"] for r in results])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

import json
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

SCOUT_JSON = Path(r"C:\Users\vamsh\.gemini\antigravity\brain\722d6332-73d9-49af-be4d-dd125c69723f\scratch\scouting.json")
OUT_JSON = Path(r"C:\Users\vamsh\.gemini\antigravity\brain\722d6332-73d9-49af-be4d-dd125c69723f\scratch\scout_deep.json")

data = json.loads(SCOUT_JSON.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
access_map = {s["siteId"]: s for s in data["access"]}

def clean_zw(s: str) -> str:
    if not s:
        return ""
    for ch in ["\u200b", "\u200c", "\u200d", "\ufeff", "\u00ad"]:
        s = s.replace(ch, "")
    return s

def dump_page(page, phase=""):
    page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")
    page.wait_for_timeout(400)
    info = {
        "phase": phase,
        "url": page.url,
        "title": clean_zw(page.title()),
        "body_text": clean_zw(page.locator("body").inner_text())[:6000],
        "elements": [],
        "iframes": []
    }
    els = page.evaluate("""() => {
        const res = [];
        document.querySelectorAll('a, button, input, select, textarea, iframe, form, table, h1, h2, h3').forEach(el => {
            res.push({
                tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
                type: el.getAttribute('type') || '',
                name: el.getAttribute('name') || '',
                id: el.id || '',
                href: el.getAttribute('href') || '',
                src: el.getAttribute('src') || '',
                value: el.value !== undefined ? String(el.value).slice(0, 100) : '',
                text: (el.innerText || '').trim().slice(0, 200)
            });
        });
        return res;
    }""")
    for e in els:
        e["text"] = clean_zw(e["text"])
        info["elements"].append(e)
    for frame in page.frames:
        if frame != page.main_frame:
            try:
                info["iframes"].append({
                    "url": frame.url,
                    "text": clean_zw(frame.locator("body").inner_text())[:4000]
                })
            except Exception as ex:
                info["iframes"].append({"url": frame.url, "error": str(ex)})
    return info

def login_and_consent(page, site):
    url = site["url"]
    creds = site["credentials"]
    page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
    page.wait_for_timeout(300)
    if page.locator('input[name="username"]').count() > 0:
        page.locator('input[name="username"]').fill(creds["username"])
        page.locator('input[name="password"]').fill(creds["password"])
        page.locator('button:has-text("Anmelden")').click()
        page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")
        page.wait_for_timeout(300)
    if "/consent" in page.url or page.locator('button:has-text("Cookies akzeptieren")').count() > 0:
        page.locator('button:has-text("Cookies akzeptieren")').first.click()
        page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")
        page.wait_for_timeout(300)
    # If landed on /notice, navigate back to root
    for _ in range(3):
        if "/notice" in page.url or "Dienst vorübergehend nicht verfügbar" in page.locator("body").inner_text():
            page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
            page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        else:
            break

results = {}

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)

    # 1. TENDER PORTAL
    ctx1 = browser.new_context()
    p1 = ctx1.new_page()
    login_and_consent(p1, access_map["tender-portal"])
    tp_steps = []
    p1.goto(access_map["tender-portal"]["url"] + "/tenders/VG-2027-7093", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
    tp_steps.append(dump_page(p1, "tender_detail"))
    results["tender-portal"] = tp_steps

    # 2. CUSTOMER PORTAL
    ctx2 = browser.new_context()
    p2 = ctx2.new_page()
    login_and_consent(p2, access_map["customer-portal"])
    cp_steps = []
    p2.goto(access_map["customer-portal"]["url"] + "/documents", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
    cp_steps.append(dump_page(p2, "documents_list"))
    results["customer-portal"] = cp_steps

    # 3. ERP
    ctx3 = browser.new_context()
    p3 = ctx3.new_page()
    login_and_consent(p3, access_map["erp"])
    erp_steps = []
    erp_steps.append(dump_page(p3, "erp_home"))
    results["erp"] = erp_steps

    # 4. MAIL
    ctx4 = browser.new_context()
    p4 = ctx4.new_page()
    login_and_consent(p4, access_map["mail"])
    mail_steps = []
    # Check how mail unlock works in the HTML
    mail_html = p4.content()
    mail_steps.append({
        "phase": "mail_raw_scripts_and_forms",
        "html_snippet": clean_zw(mail_html)[:10000]
    })
    results["mail"] = mail_steps

    browser.close()

OUT_JSON.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
print("Wrote", OUT_JSON)

import json
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

SCOUT_JSON = Path(r"C:\Users\vamsh\.gemini\antigravity\brain\722d6332-73d9-49af-be4d-dd125c69723f\scratch\scouting.json")
OUT_JSON = Path(r"C:\Users\vamsh\.gemini\antigravity\brain\722d6332-73d9-49af-be4d-dd125c69723f\scratch\scout_gates.json")

data = json.loads(SCOUT_JSON.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
access_map = {s["siteId"]: s for s in data["access"]}

def clean_zw(s: str) -> str:
    if not s:
        return ""
    for ch in ["\u200b", "\u200c", "\u200d", "\ufeff", "\u00ad"]:
        s = s.replace(ch, "")
    return s

def login_and_consent(page, site):
    url = site["url"]
    creds = site["credentials"]
    page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
    page.wait_for_timeout(300)
    if page.locator('input[name="username"]').count() > 0:
        page.locator('input[name="username"]').fill(creds["username"])
        page.locator('input[name="password"]').fill(creds["password"])
        page.locator('button:has-text("Anmelden")').click()
        page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")
        page.wait_for_timeout(300)
    if "/consent" in page.url or page.locator('button:has-text("Cookies akzeptieren")').count() > 0:
        page.locator('button:has-text("Cookies akzeptieren")').first.click()
        page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")
        page.wait_for_timeout(300)

res = {}
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)

    # Check ERP /notice HTML
    p_erp = browser.new_context().new_page()
    login_and_consent(p_erp, access_map["erp"])
    if "Dienst vorübergehend" in p_erp.locator("body").inner_text():
        p_erp.goto(access_map["erp"]["url"], wait_until="domcontentloaded")
        p_erp.wait_for_timeout(300)
    res["erp_notice_html"] = clean_zw(p_erp.content())

    # Check Mail HTML tail
    p_mail = browser.new_context().new_page()
    login_and_consent(p_mail, access_map["mail"])
    res["mail_html_tail"] = clean_zw(p_mail.content())[8000:]

    # Check Tender Portal tabs
    p_tp = browser.new_context().new_page()
    login_and_consent(p_tp, access_map["tender-portal"])
    tp_base = access_map["tender-portal"]["url"]
    res["tp_docs"] = {}
    for tab in ["documents", "questions"]:
        p_tp.goto(f"{tp_base}/tenders/VG-2027-7093?tab={tab}", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
        p_tp.wait_for_timeout(400)
        res["tp_docs"][tab] = {
            "text": clean_zw(p_tp.locator("body").inner_text()),
            "html": clean_zw(p_tp.content())
        }

    # Check Customer Portal pages 1..4
    p_cp = browser.new_context().new_page()
    login_and_consent(p_cp, access_map["customer-portal"])
    cp_base = access_map["customer-portal"]["url"]
    res["cp_pages"] = []
    for pg in range(1, 5):
        p_cp.goto(f"{cp_base}/documents?page={pg}", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
        p_cp.wait_for_timeout(300)
        res["cp_pages"].append({
            "page": pg,
            "text": clean_zw(p_cp.locator("body").inner_text()),
            "links": p_cp.evaluate("""() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a')).map(a => ({href: a.getAttribute('href'), text: a.innerText.trim()}))""")
        })

    browser.close()

OUT_JSON.write_text(json.dumps(res, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
print("Wrote", OUT_JSON)

Requesting a TAN through the web interface, expecting it to arrive at the designated webmail address. This action is the next logical step in the process, as indicated in the trace file. The TAN is needed to proceed with signing the document.

The goal is to identify and apply any quantity changes due to clarifications, ignoring any withdrawn answers, and address the unit conversions as per the rules. This requires careful parsing of each position and comparing it to the clarifications.


Analyzing tender data, focusing on the unit of measure (`Stk` or `Satz`). If the unit is `Satz`, converting to `Stück` by multiplying with the specified `pieces_per_set` defined in the specification document. This is crucial for all downstream calculations.

Determining the applicable specification revision, prioritizing the current (`gültig`) revision in the customer portal document. Ignoring any superseded revisions.

Identifying and applying any technical amendments from the Q&A, specifically those referencing both the tender reference and the current revision ID. Carefully parsing these to capture the required attributes.


Analyzing the technical specifications, specifically those with a 'nutzbarer Weg' designation and related 'Endreserve' parameters. The goal is to derive the nominal stroke, accounting for Q&A amendments, and then match the calculated value with the ERP system data.

The process involves searching the latest 'Technikfreigabe' mail, dated before or on the specified scenario date, to find the 'Endreserve-Schlüssel'.  After the nominal stroke is derived, the process moves to ERP material selection by 'Kataloggruppe'.


The search focuses on finding an active ERP material that perfectly matches the derived technical requirements (bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, and certification). Blocked materials are explicitly excluded.

A potential conflict arises if multiple active materials within the same catalog group share identical technical attributes, so the activity status for each must be checked to resolve any ambiguity.  If no matching active material is found for *any* tender position, the offer will be marked as "no_bid".


Analyzing mail content for relevant approvals, focusing on messages dated on or before the scenario date and originating from authorized senders. Discount approvals, technical releases, packaging rates, and other relevant information are being parsed from the "Nachrichtentext (Original)" section of each email. The specific fields within these approvals are being identified for application in the tender.


Analyzing price conditions in the ERP system, specifically searching for the valid price record applicable to the scenario date. The validity of the price record is verified, and the unit price, unit of measure, and currency are extracted.

Determining the applicable price scale within the condition, based on the position's final quantity, selecting the highest scale with a minimum quantity less than or equal to the position quantity. Price normalization based on the unit of measure is performed.

If the currency is not EUR, the relevant exchange rate is being searched in the latest currency fixing email available before or on the specified scenario date. The required FX rate will be applied for final calculation.


Now calculating the `base_unit_price` for each tender position, applying currency conversion and rounding as specified in the rules. This `base_unit_price` is a key input for subsequent calculations, like order-level discount thresholds and bonus calculations.

The system will now search for the most recent discount approval email from the relevant sender, matching the tender reference and date criteria. The goal is to determine if a minimum undiscounted order value is required for the discount.


Determining the applicable discount for each position. If a discount approval exists with an order value threshold, and the undiscounted order value meets or exceeds it, the specified percentage applies; otherwise, no discount is applied. Older approvals are ignored if newer ones exist.

Calculating the metal surcharge per unit based on the ERP material's `Zuschlagsmasse` and a `Preisindex`. The applicable index rate is determined by searching the latest valid email containing price indices, matching the tender reference, and selecting the rate valid on the scenario date.

Calculating mass surcharge by converting `Zuschlagsmasse` to kg and multiplying by the selected index rate. Any setup fees will be determined from Q&A data dated on or before the scenario date.


Now, assessing Q&A data for one-time setup fees, distinguishing ordinary fees from shared pool assignments (RP-...). For pool assignments, extracting the pool key to look up the total pool fee in the latest relevant email.

Calculating the weight for each pool member using final quantity and ERP material allocation weight, ensuring to use 'Umlagegewicht' in g/Stück. Proportional allocation of the total pool fee using the largest-remainder method, determining cents per position.


Allocating the pool fee using the largest remainder method, ensuring correct distribution of cents per position.  The `setup_pool_allocated` is calculated by dividing allocated cents by 100 to convert to EUR.

Calculating the unrounded `surcharge_per_unit` by summing the mass surcharge and the per-unit setup costs (ordinary setup plus pool allocation), dividing by the final quantity. This value is then rounded to the nearest cent.

Now, analyzing Q&A data for packaging rates. If a `Verpackungstarif` is present for a position, the corresponding rate will be looked up in the latest relevant packaging tariff email.


Packaging cost per unit is being calculated based on the carton rate and pieces per carton, derived from email and ERP data, respectively.  The number of cartons per position will be calculated independently and rounded up.  Undiscounted goods value for positions assigned to a bonus plan will be computed using the final quantity and base unit price. The calculation will then determine a packaging cost per unit, rounded to the nearest cent.


Calculating total eligible goods value. Then, applying the marginal percentage band calculations.

Summing band credits and rounding to the nearest cent.

Allocating the total bonus proportionally across eligible positions using the largest remainder method. Non-eligible positions receive zero rebate.


The Q&A data is being examined to identify any assigned condition groups ("K-..."). These groups are cross-referenced with the latest email containing pricing conditions ("Konditionsregeln") to determine the applicable discount. A "base_only" group discounts the base unit price, while a "base_and_surcharge" group discounts both base price and mass surcharge. A "neither" or fixed-price condition implies no discounting.


Calculating the final unit price involves summing the discounted base, discounted mass surcharge, per-unit setup costs, and carton cost, then subtracting rebates, and finally dividing by the final quantity. This unrounded price is then rounded to the nearest cent.

Total net price is determined by summing the product of final quantity and unit price for all positions, then rounding to the nearest cent.


Determining the lead time for each tender position is the current objective. A commitment key from the Q&A will be searched in the 'Terminfreigabe' mail. If the committed material matches the tender material *and* the pooled quantity is within the ceiling, the committed lead time is assigned.

If no commitment is found, the available stock from ERP is assessed. If the available stock is sufficient for the pooled quantity, the 'Lieferzeit ab Lager' lead time is applied; otherwise, 'Produktionslieferzeit' is used.

import asyncio
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(r"d:\Personal_Projects\TUM_HackathonFinal\starter-kit")))

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
from dom_helpers import login_portal, safe_goto, get_clean_text, prepare_page
from calculator import normalize_cert

s = json.load(
    open(
        r"C:\Users\vamsh\.gemini\antigravity\brain\722d6332-73d9-49af-be4d-dd125c69723f\scratch\scouting.json",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
)
tp = [a for a in s["access"] if a["siteId"] == "tender-portal"][0]


def pick_option(opts: list[dict], desired: str, is_cert: bool = False) -> str:
    non_empty = [o for o in opts if o["v"] != ""]
    if is_cert and normalize_cert(desired) == "keine":
        for o in non_empty:
            if (
                normalize_cert(o["v"]) == "keine"
                or normalize_cert(o["t"]) == "keine"
                or "ohne" in o["t"].lower()
                or "keine" in o["t"].lower()
            ):
                return o["v"]
    for o in non_empty:
        if o["v"].lower() == desired.lower() or desired.lower() in o["t"].lower() or desired.lower() in o["v"].lower():
            return o["v"]
    if len(non_empty) == 1:
        return non_empty[0]["v"]
    return desired

import asyncio
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(r"d:\Personal_Projects\TUM_HackathonFinal\starter-kit")))

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
from dom_helpers import login_portal, safe_goto, get_clean_text, prepare_page
from calculator import normalize_cert

s = json.load(
    open(
        r"C:\Users\vamsh\.gemini\antigravity\brain\722d6332-73d9-49af-be4d-dd125c69723f\scratch\scouting.json",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
)
tp = [a for a in s["access"] if a["siteId"] == "tender-portal"][0]

POS_DATA = {
    "01.01": ("80", "200", "Schwenkauge", "EN 1493", "HZ-1609", "25", "2614,68", "2743,58", "6,69", "1,59", "0,00", "2"),
    "01.02": ("63", "500", "Flansch", "EN 1493", "HZ-2170", "29", "680,37", "705,15", "5,91", "4,57", "0,00", "3"),
    "01.03": ("63", "500", "Flansch", "EN 1493", "HZ-2170", "16", "734,49", "753,23", "12,57", "4,97", "580,41", "11"),
    "01.04": ("50", "600", "Schwenkauge", "Keine", "HZ-3916", "21", "1906,85", "2107,18", "5,25", "1,26", "2131,11", "3"),
    "01.05": ("125", "300", "Flansch", "Keine", "HZ-6932", "130", "1692,74", "1866,15", "8,06", "1,94", "11683,58", "3"),
}


def pick_option(opts: list[dict], desired: str, is_cert: bool = False) -> str:
    non_empty = [o for o in opts if o["v"] != ""]
    if is_cert and normalize_cert(desired) == "keine":
        for o in non_empty:
            if (
                normalize_cert(o["v"]) == "keine"
                or normalize_cert(o["t"]) == "keine"
                or "ohne" in o["t"].lower()
                or "keine" in o["t"].lower()
            ):
                return o["v"]
    for o in non_empty:
        if o["v"].lower() == desired.lower() or desired.lower() in o["t"].lower() or desired.lower() in o["v"].lower():
            return o["v"]
    if len(non_empty) == 1:
        return non_empty[0]["v"]
    return desired


async def run():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        b = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        page = await b.new_page()
        await login_portal(page, tp)
        await safe_goto(page, tp["url"].rstrip("/") + "/tenders/VG-2027-7093")
        part = page.locator('button:has-text("Teilnahme bekunden")')
        if await part.count() > 0:
            await part.first.click()
            await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")
        await safe_goto(page, tp["url"].rstrip("/") + "/tenders/VG-2027-7093/submission")
        await prepare_page(page)
        await page.fill('input[name="company"]', "Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH")
        await page.fill('input[name="vat"]', "DE811234567")
        await page.fill('input[name="email"]', "vertrieb@linden-hydraulik.example")
        await page.click('button[name="action"][value="next"]')
        await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")
        await prepare_page(page)
        await page.select_option('select[name="kind"]', "bid")
        await page.click('button[name="action"][value="next"]')
        await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")

        for _ in range(5):
            await prepare_page(page)
            h2 = (await page.locator("h2").first.inner_text()).strip()
            pos_id = h2.replace("Position", "").strip()
            bore, stroke, mount, cert, mat, qty, price, base_p, sur, pack, reb, lead = POS_DATA[pos_id]
            for sel_name, val, is_c in [
                ("bore", bore, False),
                ("stroke", stroke, False),
                ("mounting", mount, False),
                ("certification", cert, True),
            ]:
                opts = await page.evaluate(
                    f"""() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('select[name="{sel_name}"] option')).map(o => ({{v: o.value, t: o.textContent}}))"""
                )
                target_v = pick_option(opts, val, is_c)
                await page.select_option(f'select[name="{sel_name}"]', target_v)
                await page.click('button[name="action"][value="configure"]')
                await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")
                await prepare_page(page)
            mat_opts = await page.evaluate(
                """() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('select[name="material"] option')).map(o => ({v: o.value, t: o.textContent}))"""
            )
            await page.select_option('select[name="material"]', pick_option(mat_opts, mat))
            await page.fill('input[name="quantity"]', qty)
            await page.fill('input[name="price"]', price)
            await page.fill('input[name="base_price"]', base_p)
            await page.fill('input[name="surcharge"]', sur)
            await page.fill('input[name="packaging"]', pack)
            await page.fill('input[name="rebate"]', reb)
            await page.select_option('select[name="lead"]', lead)
            await page.click('button[name="action"][value="next"]')
            await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")

        # Step 8: Konditionen
        await prepare_page(page)
        print("Step 8 text:", await get_clean_text(page))
        await page.fill('input[name="discount"]', "5")
        await page.fill('input[name="total"]', "356949,62")
        await page.click('button[name="action"][value="next"]')
        await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")

        # Step 9: Erklärungen
        await prepare_page(page)
        await page.check('input[name="acknowledge"]')
        await page.click('button[name="action"][value="next"]')
        await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")

        # Step 10: Prüfen und signieren
        await prepare_page(page)
        print("=== STEP 10 SUMMARY ===")
        print(await get_clean_text(page))
        await b.close()


asyncio.run(run())

234:         except Exception:
235:             if attempt == 3:
236:                 raise
237:             await asyncio.sleep(0.3 * (attempt + 1))
238:     return await get_clean_text(page)

266: async def paginate_pages(page, start_url: str, max_pages: int = 25) -> list[str]:
267:     """Visit `start_url` and follow 'Nächste Seite' links to collect clean text of all pages."""
268:     texts: list[str] = []
269:     current_url = start_url
270:     visited: set[str] = set()
271: 
272:     for _ in range(max_pages):
273:         if current_url in visited:
274:             break
275:         visited.add(current_url)
276:         text = await safe_goto(page, current_url)
277:         texts.append(text)
278: 
279:         # Look for Nächste Seite link
280:         next_href = await page.evaluate(
281:             """() => {
282:             const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a[href]'));
283:             for (const a of links) {
284:                 const t = (a.innerText || '').replace(/[\\u200b\\u200c\\u200d\\ufeff\\u00ad]/g, '').trim();
285:                 if (t === 'Nächste Seite' || t.includes('Nächste Seite') || t === 'Nächster Konditionssatz') {
286:                     return a.getAttribute('href');
287:                 }
288:             }
289:             return null;
290:         }"""
291:         )
292:         if not next_href:
293:             break
294:         current_url = urljoin(current_url, strip_zwc(next_href))
295: 
296:     return texts

303: def parse_tender_positions_from_text(text: str) -> list[TenderPosition]:
304:     """Extract tender positions from CSV or table/block text on the tender portal."""
305:     positions: dict[str, TenderPosition] = {}
306:     cleaned = strip_zwc(text)
307: 
308:     # 1. CSV lines: Position;Kurztext;Menge;Einheit;Anforderung -> 01.01;...;24;Stk;A-1
309:     for line in cleaned.splitlines():
310:         parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split(";")]
311:         if len(parts) >= 5 and re.match(r"^\d{2}\.\d{2}$", parts[0]):
312:             pos_id, desc, qty_s, unit, req_ref = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], parts[3], parts[4]
313:             try:
314:                 positions[pos_id] = TenderPosition(
315:                     position=pos_id,
316:                     requirement_ref=req_ref,
317:                     original_quantity=int(parse_locale_decimal(qty_s)),
318:                     unit=unit,
319:                     description=desc,
320:                 )
321:             except ValueError:
322:                 pass
323: 
324:     # 2. Tabular or block lines: Position: 01.01 ... Menge: 24 Stk ... Anforderungsreferenz: A-1
325:     block_matches = re.finditer(
326:         r"Position:\s*(\d{2}\.\d{2}).*?Menge:\s*(\d+)\s*([A-Za-zÄÖÜäöüß]+).*?Anforderungsreferenz:\s*(A-\d+)",
327:         cleaned,
328:         re.DOTALL,
329:     )
330:     for m in block_matches:
331:         pos_id, qty_s, unit, req_ref = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3), m.group(4)
332:         if pos_id not in positions:
333:             positions[pos_id] = TenderPosition(
334:                 position=pos_id,
335:                 requirement_ref=req_ref.strip(),
336:                 original_quantity=int(qty_s),
337:                 unit=unit.strip(),
338:             )
339: 
340:     # 3. Table rows: 01.01 \t ... \t 24 \t Stk \t A-1
341:     for line in cleaned.splitlines():
342:         m_row = re.search(
343:             r"\b(\d{2}\.\d{2})\b\s+([^\t\n]+?)\s+(\d+)\s+(Stk|Stück|Satz|ST)\s+(A-\d+)\b",
344:             line,
345:             re.IGNORECASE,
346:         )
347:         if m_row:
348:             pos_id, desc, qty_s, unit, req_ref = m_row.groups()
349:             if pos_id not in positions:
350:                 positions[pos_id] = TenderPosition(
351:                     position=pos_id,
352:                     requirement_ref=req_ref.strip(),
353:                     original_quantity=int(qty_s),
354:                     unit=unit.strip(),
355:                     description=desc.strip(),
356:                 )
357: 
358:     return sorted(positions.values(), key=lambda x: x.position)
